methods.notes: Beurer/Sanitas advertise the 0xFFE0 service; Medisana BS444 advertises the 0x78b2 weight service; Trisa Body Analyze 4.0 advertises 0x7802. Local names vary; openScale matches per model.

device.manufacturer: Beurer / Sanitas / SilverCrest, Medisana, Trisa (openScale documents 85 scales)
device.name: openScale-documented BLE Body Scales (Beurer/Sanitas, Medisana BS444, Trisa)
device.notes:
openScale (GPLv3) documents dozens of Bluetooth body-composition scales whose vendor apps are cloud/account-oriented; this spec captures three families openScale documents that are not already in this registry. All are local BLE reads (some need a one-time user register / time-set write) — no cloud.
BEURER / SANITAS / SilverCrest (shared platform): service 0xFFE0, characteristic 0xFFE1 (writes AND notifications). Frames start with e7/f7. Command bytes: user-ID query 0x4F, set unit 0x4D, add user 0x31, request user list 0x33, perform measurement 0x40, request saved measurements 0x41. A measurement record is 22 bytes: <timestamp><weight><impedance><fat><water> <muscle><bone><BMR><AMR><BMI>; weight = 2 bytes big-endian in g/50; impedance 2 bytes BE; unix timestamp 4 bytes.
MEDISANA BS444: weight service 000078b2-...; weight-measurement 00008a21-... (indicate), body-composition 00008a22-... (indicate), command 00008a81-... (write). Weight packet (0x8a21): byte0 flags (bits for unit kg/lb/st), bytes1-2 weight little-endian /100 for the demonstrated kg example only (lb/st divisors unresolved), bytes5-8 timestamp as seconds since 2010-01-01 LE, byte13 user-ID (1-8, 0xFF unset). Body-comp packet (0x8a22): bytes6-7 kCal LE, bytes8-9 fat% /10 (mask 0xF0), 10-11 water%, 12-13 muscle%, 14-15 bone mass. TRIGGER: write 02 7b 7b f6 0d to the command characteristic.
TRISA Body Analyze 4.0: Weight Scale Service 0x7802 (distinct from Medisana's 0x78b2); chars 0x8a20 (feature), 0x8a21 (measurement indicate), 0x8a81 (download/command write), 0x8a82 (upload indicate). Challenge-response pairing: device sends a0AABBCCDD (32-bit password) on 0x8a82; client writes 21AABBCCDD (set broadcast id) then 22 (disconnect) to 0x8a81. For reads: device sends a1AABBCCDD challenge; client replies 20<challenge XOR password> then 02<seconds since 2010-01-01 UTC, LE32>. Weight = 24-bit LE mantissa x 10^(signed 8-bit exponent).

openness.notes: The vendors do not document these; openScale reverse-engineered them and its wiki is the authoritative per-scale reference. Credit openScale — it documents dozens of scale families.

upstream_docs.covers: The full catalogue (85 scales / 59 handlers) and links to each family's protocol page.
upstream_docs.title: openScale — supported scales

pairing.notes: All three families connect without a bond. What differs is what a client must do once connected: Beurer/Sanitas/SilverCrest register a user, Medisana needs its trigger magic, and Trisa completes an XOR challenge-response against a password captured during its own first-contact handshake. None of that is BLE pairing, and a client that treats it as such will go looking for an SMP exchange that never happens.

credentials.notes: No Wi-Fi. Trisa binds a 32-bit password during pairing used in its XOR challenge-response; the others are unauthenticated local reads.
stored_on_device: Trisa: a broadcast-id / password bound during pairing

factory_reset.description:
What the manuals do give is per-user memory rather than a reset: the Medisana units hold eight user profiles with thirty measurements each, selected with the SET button, and a profile is changed by overwriting it rather than deleted.
The privacy-shaped answer, which is usually what someone reaching for a reset actually wants, is the guest slot. Weighing in guest mode stores nothing at all on the scale — and on Medisana it also disables the Bluetooth transmission, so it is not a mode to use when the point is to record a reading.
factory_reset.effect: Not established for any of the three families. The vendor manuals cover selecting and overwriting the per-user memory slots but describe no operation that clears the scale wholesale, and none of the families stores a credential or a bond that a reset would need to remove.

methods.description: Connect over BLE, subscribe to the family's measurement/indicate characteristic, and (per family) register a user, send the trigger magic, or complete the challenge-response before measurements arrive.

steps.action: Connect and subscribe to the measurement/indicate characteristic for the family.
Beurer/Sanitas: register a user (0x31) / request measurements (0x41). Medisana: write 02 7b 7b f6 0d. Trisa: complete the challenge-response.
Step on the scale; read the measurement record.

setup.notes: Local BLE read; some families need a one-time on-device write: Beurer/ Sanitas and Medisana register a user and (Medisana) require the trigger magic; Trisa uses the XOR challenge-response with a password captured during a pairing handshake. No cloud.

rejoin.notes: No network membership; a new BLE client connects (and re-registers a user) independently.

testing.notes: Not driven against hardware by this project. The service/characteristic UUIDs, command bytes and record layouts are from the openScale wiki pages for each family.

beurer_sanitas.timestamp_note: BF800 live records can set bit 31 as a flag; mask it before interpreting Unix seconds. Saved records may carry the same timestamp with the bit clear.

fields.name: flags
fields.notes: Bits 5-6 select display unit; only the kg scaling below is established.

fields.name: weight_kg
fields.notes: Valid only for the kg example; lb/st divisors remain unresolved.

reassembled_records.scope: These layouts apply only after joining the notification fragments for one complete measurement; do not parse an individual fragment by these offsets.

fields.name: flags
fields.notes: Bits 0-4 condition timestamp, resistances, user and status. Bits 5-6 select kg/lb/st; the 0x60 alias is unresolved.

fields.name: resistance_1
fields.notes: Starts after the fixed header and any timestamp already consumed; 24-bit LE mantissa plus signed exponent.

fields.name: resistance_2
fields.notes: Starts at 9 when timestamp is present but R1 is absent, at 13 when both are present, and at 5 when both are absent. 24-bit LE mantissa plus signed exponent.

fields.name: reserved
fields.offset_formula: 19 only when all optional fields are present
fields.presence: full example only; trailing role/length not established for shorter records

trisa_body_analyze.layout: Five fixed bytes followed by compact flag-conditioned fields in timestamp, resistance-1, resistance-2, user, status order. The full 20-byte example is not a universal record length.

characteristics.name: Command / measurement
characteristics.notes: Both the command write channel and the measurement notification channel.

services.name: Beurer / Sanitas scale service
services.notes: Writes and notifications both on 0xFFE1. Frames start e7/f7. Commands: 0x4F user-ID query, 0x4D set unit, 0x31 add user, 0x33 request users, 0x40 perform measurement, 0x41 request saved measurements. 22-byte record: timestamp, weight (BE, g/50), impedance, fat, water, muscle, bone, BMR, AMR, BMI.

characteristics.name: Weight measurement (indicate)
characteristics.notes: Medisana: byte0 flags (unit), bytes1-2 weight LE /100 for the kg example only, bytes5-8 seconds since 2010 LE, byte13 user-ID. Do not generalize that divisor to lb/st. Trisa: weight = 24-bit LE mantissa x 10^(signed 8-bit exponent). Full reassembled layouts are under protocol_details.reassembled_records.

characteristics.name: Body composition (indicate, Medisana)
characteristics.notes: bytes6-7 kCal LE, 8-9 fat% /10 (mask 0xF0), 10-11 water%, 12-13 muscle%, 14-15 bone mass.

characteristics.name: Command (write)
characteristics.notes: Medisana trigger: write 02 7b 7b f6 0d. Trisa: 21AABBCCDD set broadcast-id, 22 disconnect, 20<challenge XOR password>, 02<seconds since 2010 LE32>.

services.name: Medisana BS444 weight service (0x78b2)
services.notes: Medisana BS444 (service 0x78b2): weight 0x8a21 (indicate), body-comp 0x8a22 (indicate), command 0x8a81 (write; trigger 02 7b 7b f6 0d). NOTE: the Trisa Body Analyze 4.0 exposes the SAME 0x8a2x characteristic UUIDs (feature 0x8a20, measurement 0x8a21 indicate, command 0x8a81 write, upload 0x8a82 indicate; challenge-response) but under its own weight service 0x7802, NOT 0x78b2 — resolve the characteristics by UUID. Timestamps use epoch 2010.
